kai: Heads-up — we're seeing a short burst of correctable ECCs on pool-us-west-2-gpu-pool-12 starting ~2005123300. Spike is noisy (lots of short bursts across cards) rather than single-card ramp. telemetry shows ~95 corr/min peaked, usually baseline 2-4/min. wondering ops preference: immediate soft-evac vs widen threshold + extra sampling?
sasha: Can you paste the aggregate metric and the per-card breakdown?
kai: sure, quick snapshot:
```
metric: gpu.ecc.correctable.rate
pool: us-west-2-gpu-pool-12
window: 1m
aggregate: 95/min
card-0: 28/min
card-1: 2/min
card-2: 31/min
card-3: 14/min
card-4: 18/min
burstiness: high (p90 p50 ratio ~9)
```
Also noticed the cards with higher rates map to PCIe slots 3/5 on the node chassis.
alex-m: hmm correlation to PCIe slots is interesting — we saw similar last quarter where slot wiring + power ripple manifested as noisy ECCs. Did we also see increased Xid64 or Xid13 (uncorrectable) counters?
kai: no Xids, only correctables. No dropouts. Kernel logs are clean except these: 
```
[GPU ERR] GPU0: correctable ECC 12 events (0x2)
[GPU ERR] GPU2: correctable ECC 15 events (0x2)
```
jordan: Given it's correctables and bursty, I lean towards widening the transient threshold and creating a short-lived noisy-card annotation rather than immediate evac. Full drain/replace causes capacity pain in us-west-2 right now.
infra-bot: Alert created: INC-2341. Current threshold 50/min per-pool, evaluated over 1m.
sasha: What's our current auto-drain logic? I thought we soft-drain after 3 windows over threshold and full drain after 5.
maria-p: yeah current flow: annotate -> soft-drain (stop new allocations, keep existing for 30s) after 3 consecutive 1m windows >50; hard-evac after 5 windows or any uncorrectable/Xid event.
alex-m: Proposal: update policy to be more burst-aware: require sustained >threshold over a decaying window (e.g., exponentially weighted moving average over 5m) and add a per-card slot correlation check. If two cards on same PCIe domain spike within 2 minutes, prefer hardware flagging and notify HW vendor instead of immediate replacement.
jordan: That seems reasonable. Need to quantify SLO impact cost of delaying evacuations: current node handles ~12x small jobs, if we soft-drain we lose immediate bin-packing but avoid expensive replacement (~$3k/card + logistics).
kai: Also suggest increasing sample windows for pool-level thresholds when cluster is at <10% free capacity in region — avoid cascade drains. We're at 6% free GPUs in us-west-2 today.
sasha: Is there any temporary mitigation we can try remotely? e.g., reduce GPU clocks or toggle ECC mode?
alex-m: Toggling ECC off isn't allowed for customer workloads. We can try light-weight firmware reset on affected cards (non-disruptive) via nvlink reset path, but that requires rebooting drivers on node - will cause short GC pauses. Not ideal.
infra-bot: Runbook snippet attached: `soft-evac-flow v1` -> annotate -> 5m grace -> soft-drain -> 15m monitor -> escalate to hard-evac if sustained.
maria-p: If we widen thresholds we should add better visibility: add p95 burst metric and pci-slot tagging to dashboards so reviewers can see domain-level noise.
jordan: Agreed. I can implement the EWMA gating change in the spike-detector lambda. Quick pseudo: 
```
alpha = 0.33
ewma_t = alpha * current_rate + (1-alpha) * ewma_prev
trigger if ewma_t > threshold
```
Also add requirement: must be >threshold for 3 consecutive ewma samples (1m cadence).
kai: timeline request: can we roll the detector change as a config flag today and run in dry-run for 2 hours? If it matches what we saw in past noisy bursts, we can flip.
sasha: Dry-run + dashboard overlays sound good. Also create a short-term capacity workaround: enable cross-region burst to us-east-1 for non-urgent ML jobs to free up ~10% capacity — ops can toggle via placement policy.
alex-m: I'll coordinate vendor contact if slot correlation persists post-rollout. If vendor confirms board-level issue, we'll schedule replacement in next maintenance window.
infra-bot: Action items created: A1 (kai) collect PCIe mapping + per-node kernel logs; A2 (jordan) implement EWMA dry-run flag; A3 (maria-p) add p95 burst + pci-slot to dashboard; A4 (sasha) enable cross-region burst for non-urgent jobs.
kai: I'll attach per-node mapping in the incident ticket. Quick note: if EWMA misses a true slow ramp (not a burst), we should still trigger via existing full-evac on uncorrectables, so that safety net remains.
sasha: SGTM. If dry-run shows EWMA ignoring real sustained ramps, revert.
jordan: Deploying dry-run now to lambda namespace: spike-detector:ewma-rollout=canary. Will collect annotations to /infra/ewma/dryrun/logs.
infra-bot: spike-detector canary deployed at 2005123465. Dry-run collecting events; will report in 1m.
kai: thanks — watching the dashboards. I'll update here in 10m after we get a few more windows. :eyes:
